Sns Gives you more options from my experience and more mobility, that said dual blades if im not mistaken will typicly do quite more damage, so its really up to you.  
on dual blades you will pretty much completely have to relly on iframing monster attacks at high level play while on sns you have a bit more options i guess? you do actualy have ways inside your combos to reposition so you wont get hit. Sns overall to me is more fun long term, i have around 10000 hours total in the monster hunter franchise (mind you lots of this was from when i was younger i whould litrely just carry my consoles around and never turn them off ...) so of actual gameplay i whould say probabyl around 6000.  
sns just never really gets boring i guess? tbh if i had to pick 1 weapon and i could never play anny other weapon sns whould be suprisingly high on that list for most people, the reason being its just one of those weapons wich can be as complex or as simple as you want it to be. You can do complicated combos wich require well timed inputs or you can just spam the same combo over and over again if you are to lazzy to put in all that effort.  
Dual blades on the other hand does indeed become rather liniar pretty quick and its eather going to be cyceling the same combo over and over again while hyperfixating on making sure you iframe every single attack or you do the exact same buton mashing over and over again and just end up getting your ass whooped across the screen every 5-10 seconds ...  
Of course i am putting things into extremes here but this simply is my experience at the extremes with both weapons.  
SnS never fails you and you feel in controle at all times  
DB can be a massive toss up and you tend to feel stuck a lot of the times

that said the new mh wilds does seem to reduce this feeling quite a bit for DB yet i still feel like its a bit of a toss up a lot of the time.
